messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: exporter-heartbeat-jitter > 500ms for otel-exporter-prod, redispatch-queue length rising, dropped_spans increased ~12% in last 5m
maya: seeing it too on dashboard, latency spikes then exporter restart events. can we map to a deploy? :eyes:
rahul: no deploys in the last hour from infra. metrics show exporter process CPU spiking then long GC pauses, then heartbeat misses.
jordan: quick check: traces that are missing children look like they had partial flushes. tracing-bot attached an example trace id 1f2a3b below.
tracing-bot: sample trace 1f2a3b: root span present, several downstream service spans absent, last seen outbound span has no traceparent header in logs.
sara: interesting — our ingress proxy did a config reload ~10m ago, but reloads are usually safe. could the proxy be trimming headers on retry?
leo: I pulled exporter logs; pattern looks like exporter marks peer unhealthy (heartbeat timeout) and triggers redispatch, which re-queues spans. if the in-memory buffer is full we drop older spans. see log snippet:```
2026-03-20T10:12:34Z exporter main: heartbeat latency=612ms
2026-03-20T10:12:34Z exporter buffer: pending=4230 capacity=5000
2026-03-20T10:12:35Z exporter main: GC pause 340ms
2026-03-20T10:12:35Z exporter client: mark_unhealthy peer=kafka-telemetry/10.2.4.7
2026-03-20T10:12:36Z exporter redispatcher: requeue=380 dropped=120
```
maya: so root cause could be exporter GC pauses + heartbeat threshold too tight causing churn and buffer overflow. any quick mitigation?
rahul: immediate mitigations: 1) raise heartbeat threshold from 300ms -> 1s temporarily, 2) increase exporter buffer capacity to 10k, 3) scale exporter instances by +2 to reduce per-instance load. I can push heat-of-the-moment flags.
jordan: agree. also add short-term config to disable aggressive redispatch backoff so we don't thrash the queue.
sara: does anyone think this could be caused by the retention TTL eviction timing? we saw TTL sweeps at 10:00 that removed queued spans older than 30s.
leo: TTL is independent — eviction happens when retention service sees span.age > configured_ttl. but if redispatch pushes timestamps forward incorrectly, it could look old. worth adding metric for redispatch_age.
tracing-bot: reproduced missing-span pattern in dev environment by simulating a 300ms pause in exporter process. when pause >250ms and heartbeat threshold=300ms, exporter gets marked unhealthy and re-registers, causing duplicate inflight markers; consumer code drops duplicates and orphans child spans.
maya: ok let's make the quick config changes. rahul, can you open a small config PR and roll to canary? leo, monitor redispatch queue and dropped_spans. set alert bump to P1 if dropped_spans > 5% of incoming.
rahul: will open PR now, canary to 2 instances in us-west first. rollback if errors.
leo: monitoring: added temporary grafana panel for exporter.redispatch.age and exporter.heartbeat.latency, and a threshold alert.
sara: also add a tracing rule to log raw incoming headers for a sample of 1% so we can see if traceparent disappears before exporter. make sure it's redacted for PII.
jordan: after hotfix, we should schedule a postmortem to decide long-term: tune GC (move to G1), bump buffer defaults, and make heartbeat smarter (consider probing non-blocking).
rahul: PR merged to canary, promoting now. fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:
leo: metrics trending down after canary: heartbeat p95 dropped from 480ms -> 120ms, dropped_spans down to 1.4%. scaling up next.
maya: thanks all. create incident ticket and assign follow-up owners: rahul (hotfix), sara (ingress header audit), jordan (tracing reliability), leo (monitoring & dashboards).
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026-234 exporter-heartbeat-jitter, severity=P2, owners=[rahul,sara,jordan,leo]
rahul: will keep thread updated. planning a full revert if canary deviates.
leo: note for postmortem: check if any rpc keepalive settings were changed in last infra patch (proto: keepalive_interval lowered).
maya: moving to #incidents for paging the oncall and then we'll update runbook. thanks everyone :shipit:
